Subject: Console concierge: compact snapshot + owner atlas for per-route economics

Team —

Quick product ask to align on a small, high-leverage Console addition I want to scope for Q1: a "concierge snapshot" tile that surfaces per-route economic signals + an owner atlas that makes handoffs and postmortems faster. Motivation: support and sales teams are spending 30–60m per incident mapping route names to owners and confirming the right playbook. We should automate the first-pass so an oncall or SE can act immediately.

Desired tile contents (compact):
- Route display name + canonical path id (single-line)
- 7d rolling cost ($) and % delta vs prior week
- P95 tail latency (ms) and % delta
- Top contributing token bucket or model variant (short label)
- Owner(s) + owner role (team or person) with link to owner_atlas
- One-click suggested playbook (low/medium/high priority) with rationale snippet

I attached a quick mockup and a CSV draft of the owner atlas. Questions to resolve in this thread:
1) Data feasibility: can we compute 7d rolling cost + p95 with sub-minute freshness without blowing query budgets?
2) Naming and canonicalization: we have inconsistent route naming (tenant-prefixed vs friendly names). Where should the mapping live?
3) UX constraints: tile size, truncation rules, and linkouts to full Route Inspector.
4) Ownership signals: should owner come from team metadata (service registry) or be derived from last-deployer / PATH tag?

Ask: Marissa / Kim — can you triage feasibility? Grace / Marcus — can you weigh in on owner signals and recommended playbook taxonomy?

Thanks,
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Director, Product — Console & Observability
Redwood Inference

Aditya —

Thanks for the clear ask and mockup. Quick notes from infra/observability POV:
- Cost: we already emit per-request token counts and model variant labels into the ingestion pipeline. Computing 7d rolling cost is doable as a nightly rollup and a lightweight streaming counter for last-24h. Sub-minute freshness for P95 is harder unless we accept a ~5m aggregation window. We can prototype a 1h window for Q1.
- Query budget: we should avoid heavy ad-hoc queries from the Console. Plan: precompute a daily summary and keep a 5m hot cache for the 1h sliding window. That meets most oncall needs without large egress.
- Route canonicalization: we have three competing keys (route_path, display_name, tenant_tag). I recommend we index by route_path (stable id) and maintain a small alias table for display_name. The table can be updated by a simple UI or via API.

I'll spin up a quick spike to estimate storage/cost impact and attach notes.

Marissa
Sr. Engineering Manager, Observability

Couple of practical items from SRE/ops side:
- Owner signals: the most reliable is the service registry team->owner mapping. Last-deployer is noisy (many infra deployers). If product wants user-editable aliasing, we should store that in a lightweight Owner Atlas (CSV/API) and fall back to registry.
- Playbook suggestions: we can create three canned playbooks (cost spike, latency spike, token-regression) and run a simple rule engine to pick the best candidate and a confidence score. Low lift to implement.
- Privacy: ensure owner emails are redacted in public views; show team name + pager channel.

I can help scope the rule engine and owner's sync cadence.

Kim
SRE Manager
